module_title: Introduction to Aluminum Windows and Doors

lessons.title: Why Aluminum is Popular in African Construction
lessons.body:
Aluminum windows and doors are everywhere in Africa, from Lagos to Nairobi to Johannesburg. The main reason is that aluminum does not rust like steel or rot like wood. In humid coastal cities like Mombasa or Accra, steel windows can rust through in two or three years. Aluminum, on the other hand, forms a thin protective oxide layer that stops corrosion. It also handles heavy rain and intense sun without warping or cracking. That is why most new apartment blocks, schools, and offices in Africa specify aluminum frames.

Another big factor is cost and availability. Aluminum profiles are made locally in many African countries, including Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, and Egypt. A standard 6-meter length of powder-coated aluminum profile costs between $15 and $30, depending on the thickness and finish. That is cheaper than good quality hardwood, which can cost $40 or more per meter and needs regular painting. Aluminum also comes in many colorsâwhite, bronze, black, and wood-grain finishesâso customers can match their home style without extra work.

Aluminum is also lightweight, which makes it easy to transport and install. Two workers can carry a full window frame up three floors without a crane. It does not need heavy hinges or special foundations. And because it is strong for its weight, you can make large sliding doorsâup to 3 meters wideâthat open smoothly with just one finger. This is perfect for African homes that want wide openings to let in breeze and light.

Finally, aluminum is low maintenance. You do not need to paint it every year. Just wash it with soapy water and a soft cloth every few months. It does not attract termites, and it will not burn in a fire. For a small workshop, this means you can offer customers a product that lasts 20 years or more with almost no upkeep. That is a strong selling point in any community.

lessons.title: Common Window and Door Types in African Homes
lessons.body:
When you start working with aluminum, you will mostly build four types of windows and three types of doors. Knowing these will help you talk to customers and plan your materials. The most common window is the sliding window. It has two or three panels that slide horizontally on a track. A standard sliding window for a bedroom is 1.2 meters wide by 1.2 meters high. It uses two glass panes, each about 60 cm wide, and a top and bottom track. Sliding windows are cheap and easy to install, but they only open half way.

The second type is the casement window. This is a window that opens outward like a door, using hinges on the side. It can be single or double. A casement window gives full ventilation and a tight seal when closed. It is common in bungalows and upstairs rooms. You need handles and stays to hold it open. The third type is the awning window, which opens outward from the top. It is good for rain protection because you can leave it open during light rain. The fourth type is the fixed window, which does not open at all. It is just a frame with glass, used for bathrooms or above doors for light.

For doors, the most popular is the sliding door. This is a large glass door that slides on a bottom track. A typical sliding door for a living room is 2.4 meters wide and 2.1 meters high, with two panels. It is heavy, so you need strong tracks and rollers. The second type is the hinged door, which can be single or double. A single hinged door is usually 0.9 meters wide and 2.1 meters high. It is used for entrances and bedrooms. The third type is the folding door, which has several panels that fold back like an accordion. It is used for wide openings to a patio or veranda.

In African homes, you will also see combination frames: a sliding window with a fixed top light, or a door with a small window beside it. Always measure the opening carefully. Remember that aluminum frames need a 5-10 mm gap around them for expansion and for fixing. Use a tape measure and write down width and height in millimeters. This will save you from costly mistakes.

lessons.title: Tools and Materials Needed to Get Started
lessons.body:
To start an aluminum window and door workshop, you need a basic set of hand tools and a few power tools. You do not need everything at once. Start with what you can afford and add as you get jobs. The most important tool is a miter saw. This is a power saw that cuts aluminum profiles at precise angles, usually 45 degrees for corners. A good 10-inch miter saw with a carbide-tipped blade for aluminum costs between $150 and $300. If you cannot afford one yet, you can use a hacksaw with a fine-tooth blade (32 teeth per inch) and a miter box, but it will be slower and less accurate.

Next, you need a drill. A cordless drill with a 13mm chuck is fine. You will use it to drill holes for screws and to drive self-tapping screws. Get a set of high-speed steel (HSS) drill bits. For aluminum, use a drill speed of about 1,500 to 3,000 RPM and a little kerosene or soapy water as lubricant. You also need a screwdriver set, a tape measure (5 meters is enough), a try square, a spirit level (600mm), and a center punch. A rubber mallet is useful for tapping frames together without damaging the finish.

For materials, you will need aluminum profiles. The most common are 40mm or 50mm square tubes for frames, and T-profiles for tracks. Buy from a local supplier who sells in 6-meter lengths. You also need glass. For windows, use 4mm or 6mm clear or tinted glass. For doors, use 6mm or 8mm tempered glass for safety. Other materials include: self-tapping screws (8mm and 10mm long), silicone sealant, rubber gaskets, rollers for sliding windows and doors, handles, hinges, and corner cleats. A good supplier will sell you a starter kit.

Finally, you need a workbench. Build a sturdy table 2.4 meters long and 1 meter wide, with a flat top. You can make it from plywood and 2x4 timber. Fix a vice to one corner. Keep your tools organized on a pegboard. Always buy quality blades and bitsâcheap ones break and cost more in the long run. With these tools and materials, you can build your first window in a day.

lessons.title: Safety Gear and Safe Work Practices
lessons.body:
Aluminum work involves sharp edges, flying chips, and heavy glass. Safety is not optional. Before you start any job, put on your safety gear. The most important item is safety glasses. When you cut or drill aluminum, small metal chips fly off at high speed. These can blind you. Buy a pair of clear polycarbonate safety glasses for $5. Wear them every time you use a power tool. For cutting glass, you also need safety glasses and gloves.

Gloves are next. Use leather gloves or cut-resistant gloves when handling aluminum profiles and glass. The cut edges of aluminum are razor sharp. A simple slip can slice your hand to the bone. Keep a first aid kit in your workshop with bandages, antiseptic, and eye wash. For ear protection, use ear plugs or muffs when using a miter saw or drill. The noise can damage your hearing over time. And always wear closed-toe shoes, not sandals. A falling piece of aluminum or glass can break your toes.

Safe work practices start with your workspace. Keep the floor clean and dry. Sweep up metal shavings and glass bits immediately. Do not leave tools on the floor. Make sure your workbench is stable. When using a miter saw, clamp the aluminum profile firmly against the fence. Never hold it with your hand. Let the saw reach full speed before cutting. Do not force the bladeâlet it cut at its own pace. After cutting, wait for the blade to stop completely before lifting the saw arm.

When drilling, use a clamp or vice to hold the workpiece. Never drill into a piece you are holding with your hand. Use a drill bit designed for metal. If the bit grabs, release the trigger immediately. For glass handling, always wear gloves and carry glass vertically, not flat. Store glass in a rack with padding. Never stack glass on the floor where someone can step on it. If you are working at height, use a sturdy ladder and have someone hold it. Never rush. Most accidents happen when you are tired or trying to finish quickly. Take breaks, and keep your phone away. A safe workshop is a productive workshop.

lessons.title: Setting Up a Small Workshop in Your Community
lessons.body:
You do not need a big factory to start. Many successful aluminum fabricators in Africa started in a single garage or a rented 3m x 4m room. The key is to find a space that is secure, has power, and is accessible to customers. Look for a location near a main road or a growing residential area. A small shop in a market center or near a hardware store is ideal. You can rent a space for as little as $50 to $150 per month in many African towns. Make sure the landlord allows light industrial workâsome residential areas have noise restrictions.

Your workshop needs three zones: a cutting area, an assembly area, and a storage area. The cutting area should have your miter saw on a sturdy bench. Put a rubber mat under the saw to reduce vibration. The assembly area needs a large flat table (2.4m x 1m) where you can lay out frames. The storage area is for aluminum profiles, glass, and finished products. Store aluminum profiles horizontally on racks, not leaning against a wall, to prevent bending. Glass should be stored vertically in a wooden rack with slots. Keep everything off the floor.

Power supply is critical. You need at least one 13-amp socket for the miter saw and one for the drill. If your area has frequent power cuts, buy a small generator (2-3 kVA) for $200-$400. That will keep you working. Lighting should be brightâuse LED tubes over your workbench. Ventilation is also important, especially when using silicone or cleaning solvents. Install a small exhaust fan or keep a window open.

Marketing your workshop is simple. Put a signboard outside with your business name and phone number. Tell local hardware stores and glass suppliers that you are available. Offer to make a sample window or door for a neighbor at a discount in exchange for a testimonial. Join local WhatsApp groups for builders and homeowners. Word of mouth is powerful. As you get jobs, reinvest in better tools. Start with one employeeâa helperâand train them. Within six months, you can be making a profit. Keep your prices competitive but do not undercharge. A standard sliding window (1.2m x 1.2m) should sell for $80 to $150, depending on glass and finish.

lessons.title: Understanding Customer Needs and Local Preferences
lessons.body:
When a customer comes to you for a window or door, they often do not know exactly what they want. Your job is to ask the right questions and listen. Start with the purpose of the opening. Is it for a bedroom, living room, bathroom, or shop? Bedrooms usually need privacy, so consider frosted glass or curtains. Living rooms want wide openings for light and breeze. Bathrooms need small, high windows for ventilation. Shops may want large display windows or sliding doors that open fully.

Next, ask about the size of the opening. Always visit the site and measure yourself. Do not trust the customer's measurements. Use a tape measure and note the width and height in millimeters. Also check the wall type: is it concrete, brick, or wood? This affects how you fix the frame. For concrete, you use expansion bolts. For brick, you may need to drill and use wall plugs. For wood, you can screw directly. Also check if the wall is straight and plumb. If not, you may need to adjust the frame with packing shims.

Local preferences vary across Africa. In coastal areas, people prefer aluminum because it resists salt air. In hot dry regions, they want reflective or tinted glass to reduce heat. In cities, white and bronze are the most popular colors. In rural areas, customers may prefer cheaper clear glass and simple designs. Some communities prefer sliding windows because they are easy to open and do not block the veranda. Others prefer casement windows for maximum airflow. Ask about security: do they want burglar bars? Many customers will want them, so you can offer to install them as an add-on.

Finally, discuss budget and timeline. Be honest about what you can deliver. A standard sliding window takes 2-3 days to fabricate and install. A large sliding door takes 4-5 days. Give a written quote that includes materials, labor, and installation. Do not forget to add 10% for unforeseen issues. After installation, show the customer how to clean and maintain the aluminum. Ask for feedback and a referral. Happy customers will bring you more work. Remember, your reputation is built on quality and honesty.

quiz.q: Why is aluminum preferred over steel for windows in coastal African cities?
options: D) It is easier to paint
quiz.explanation: Aluminum forms a protective oxide layer that prevents corrosion from salt air and humidity.

quiz.q: What is a common thickness for aluminum window frames?
quiz.explanation: 40mm and 50mm square tubes are standard for window and door frames.

quiz.q: Which window type opens outward like a door?
quiz.explanation: Casement windows are hinged on the side and open outward.

quiz.q: What is the typical width of a single hinged door?
quiz.explanation: A standard single hinged door is 0.9 meters wide and 2.1 meters high.

quiz.q: Which tool is most important for cutting aluminum profiles at precise angles?
quiz.explanation: A miter saw with a carbide-tipped blade cuts aluminum at accurate 45-degree angles.

quiz.q: What speed should you use when drilling aluminum?
quiz.explanation: Aluminum drills best at 1,500 to 3,000 RPM with lubrication.

quiz.q: What type of glass is recommended for doors for safety?
quiz.explanation: 6mm or 8mm tempered glass is stronger and breaks into small, less dangerous pieces.

quiz.q: What should you wear to protect your eyes when cutting aluminum?
quiz.explanation: Safety glasses protect against flying metal chips and glass shards.

quiz.q: Why should you clamp the aluminum profile when using a miter saw?
options: B) To prevent it from moving
C) To make the cut faster
quiz.explanation: Clamping holds the profile firmly so it does not slip and cause injury or bad cuts.

quiz.q: What is the ideal size for a small workshop?
quiz.explanation: A 3m x 4m room can accommodate cutting, assembly, and storage zones.

quiz.q: How should aluminum profiles be stored?
quiz.explanation: Horizontal storage on racks prevents bending and warping.

quiz.q: What is a good marketing strategy for a new workshop?
options: A) Wait for customers to come
C) Word of mouth and local signboard
quiz.explanation: Local signboards and referrals are effective and low-cost for community businesses.

quiz.q: What should you ask a customer first when they request a window?
options: B) The purpose of the opening
quiz.explanation: Knowing the purpose (bedroom, living room, etc.) guides the design and glass choice.

quiz.q: Why is it important to measure the opening yourself?
options: A) Customers often give wrong measurements
B) It is a legal requirement
quiz.explanation: Accurate on-site measurements prevent costly fabrication errors.

quiz.q: What is a common local preference in hot dry regions?
quiz.explanation: Tinted or reflective glass reduces heat gain from intense sunlight.

quiz.q: What should be included in a written quote?
quiz.explanation: A complete quote covers materials, labor, installation, and a contingency.

quiz.q: What is the typical selling price for a standard sliding window (1.2m x 1.2m)?
quiz.explanation: Depending on glass and finish, a standard sliding window sells for $80 to $150.

quiz.q: Which window type provides full ventilation and a tight seal when closed?
quiz.explanation: Casement windows open fully and seal tightly against weather when closed.

quiz.q: What is a common material for making aluminum profiles in Africa?
options: B) Locally made in countries like Nigeria and Kenya
quiz.explanation: Many African countries have local aluminum extrusion plants.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a rubber gasket in aluminum windows?
options: A) To make it look nice
B) To seal against water and air
quiz.explanation: Gaskets provide a weather seal and reduce noise and dust entry.

quiz.q: How often should aluminum windows be cleaned?
quiz.explanation: Washing with soapy water every few months keeps aluminum looking new.

quiz.q: What is a safe practice when handling glass?
options: B) Carry it vertically with gloves
C) Stack it on the floor
quiz.explanation: Carrying glass vertically with gloves reduces the risk of breakage and cuts.

quiz.q: What should you do if you cannot afford a miter saw initially?
options: B) Use a hacksaw with a miter box
quiz.explanation: A hacksaw with a fine-tooth blade and miter box is a low-cost alternative for accurate cuts.

quiz.q: What is the recommended gap around an aluminum frame for expansion?
quiz.explanation: A 5-10mm gap allows for thermal expansion and fixing.

quiz.q: Which color is most popular for aluminum windows in African cities?
quiz.explanation: White and bronze are the most common and widely available finishes.

quiz.q: What add-on do many customers request for security?
quiz.explanation: Burglar bars are a common security addition for windows and doors.

quiz.q: How long does it take to fabricate and install a standard sliding window?
quiz.explanation: A standard sliding window takes about 2-3 days from fabrication to installation.

quiz.q: What is a good way to get your first customers?
options: A) Offer a discount to a neighbor for a testimonial
quiz.explanation: A discounted sample job can generate word-of-mouth referrals.

quiz.q: What should you do after installing an aluminum window?
options: B) Show the customer how to clean and maintain it
C) Ask for full payment only
quiz.explanation: Teaching maintenance ensures customer satisfaction and future referrals.

quiz.q: Why is ventilation important in an aluminum workshop?
options: B) To remove fumes from silicone and solvents
quiz.explanation: Proper ventilation removes harmful fumes from adhesives and cleaning agents.
